knowledge_point.title: Applying Row Operations To a Coefficients Matrix

question.:question/problem:
Consider the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}4 & -8 & -6 \\ 7 & -8 & 4 \\ -8 & 8 & 8\end{bmatrix}.
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{1}\leftrightarrow{R}_{3}$ on $A?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The operation ${R}_{1}\leftrightarrow{R}_{3}$ means that we need to swap the first and third rows.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}4 & -8 & -6 \\ 7 & -8 & 4 \\ -8 & 8 & 8\end{bmatrix}\quad {R}_{1}\leftrightarrow{R}_{3} \\ & \sim \begin{bmatrix}-8 & 8 & 8 \\ 7 & -8 & 4 \\ 4 & -8 & -6\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}-8 & -2 & 9 \\ -3 & -8 & -6 \\ -6 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3}$ on $A?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The operation ${R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3}$ means that we need to multiply the third row of the matrix by $\frac{1}{2}.$

Multiplying the third row by $\frac{1}{2}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}-8 & -2 & 9 \\ -3 & -8 & -6 \\ -6 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}\quad {R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\ & \sim \begin{bmatrix}-8 & -2 & 9 \\ -3 & -8 & -6 \\ \frac{1}{2}\cdot (-6) & \frac{1}{2}\cdot (0) & \frac{1}{2}\cdot (0)\end{bmatrix} \\ & \sim \begin{bmatrix}-8 & -2 & 9 \\ -3 & -8 & -6 \\ -3 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:

question.:question/worked-solution:
The operation ${R}_{1}:=-2{R}_{1}$ means that we need to multiply the first row of the matrix by $-2.$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}-6 & -6 & 0 \\ -8 & 9 & 8 \\ -3 & -6 & -9\end{bmatrix}\quad {R}_{1}:=-2{R}_{1} \\ & \sim \begin{bmatrix}-2\cdot (-6) & -2\cdot (-6) & -2\cdot (0) \\ -8 & 9 & 8 \\ -3 & -6 & -9\end{bmatrix} \\ & \sim \begin{bmatrix}12 & 12 & 0 \\ -8 & 9 & 8 \\ -3 & -6 & -9\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & -6 \\ -8 & -7 & -3 \\ 6 & -6 & -5\end{bmatrix}.
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{1}:=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1}$ on $A?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The operation ${R}_{1}:=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1}$ means that we need to multiply the first row of the matrix by $-\frac{1}{2}.$

Multiplying the first row by $-\frac{1}{2}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & -6 \\ -8 & -7 & -3 \\ 6 & -6 & -5\end{bmatrix}\quad {R}_{1}:=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\ & \sim \begin{bmatrix}-\frac{1}{2}\cdot (0) & -\frac{1}{2}\cdot (0) & -\frac{1}{2}\cdot (-6) \\ -8 & -7 & -3 \\ 6 & -6 & -5\end{bmatrix} \\ & \sim \begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 3 \\ -8 & -7 & -3 \\ 6 & -6 & -5\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$
